items.markdown:
The Hebrew letter [Kaf / Chaf](https://www.chabad.org/library/article_cdo/aid/137083/jewish/Kaf-Chaf.htm) (`כ` / `ך` ) is the `11th letter of the Hebrew alphabet`.[[1]](https://www.chabad.org/library/article_cdo/aid/137083/jewish/Kaf-Chaf.htm)

### Key Facts

- **Numerical Value (Gematria):** 20 (and 500 for the final form).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaph)
- **Meaning:** "Palm of the hand," "spoon," or "vessel". It originates from a pictograph of an open hand.[[1]](https://objectivetranslation.home.blog/2019/05/26/the-amazing-biblical-language-the-importance-of-the-letter-kaf/)[[2]](https://www.balashon.com/2006/10/kaf.html)
- **Pronunciation:** 
	- With a dot inside (dagesh), it sounds like a hard **"K"** (as in *kit*).
	- Without a dot, it sounds like a soft **"Kh" or "Ch"** (as in the Scottish *loch* or German *bach*).[[1]](https://www.etz-hayim.com/hebrew/letters_and_vowels/kaf.php)
- **Forms:** 
	- **Standard (כ):** Used at the beginning or middle of a word; shaped like a curved palm or bowl.
	- **Final / Sofit (ך):** Used only at the very end of a word, written with a straight, descending line.[[1]](https://www.chabad.org/library/article_cdo/aid/137083/jewish/Kaf-Chaf.htm)[[2]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=btXfkvjS3vs)

### Symbolism and Significance

- **Vessel and Action:** A palm acts as a container or tool to hold, weigh, or give. In Jewish mysticism, it represents the bridge between *koach* (potential) and *poel* (actualization)—bringing spiritual intent into physical action.[[1]](https://inner.org/hebleter/kaf.htm)[[2]](https://gabrielelevy.com/pages/the-letter-kaf)[[3]](https://hebrew.learnoutlive.com/the-letter-kaf-as-a-metaphor/)
- **Grammar:** As a prefix, *kaf* means "like," "as," or "according to" (e.g., *ka-melekh* , meaning "like a king"). As a suffix, it denotes the second-person singular possessive ("your").[[1]](https://www.hebrew4christians.com/Grammar/Unit_One/Aleph-Bet/Kaf/kaf.html)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaph)
